disorder-name.detail: DSM-IV schizophrenia; patients had to fulfill DSM-IV criteria for schizophrenia at both baseline and follow-up. Recruited from two cohorts: Utrecht Schizophrenia project and GROUP consortium.
disorder-name.supporting_text: "we included images of patients who fulfilled DSM-IV criteria for schizophrenia both at baseline and follow-up"

dataset-of-origin.detail: Two longitudinal cohorts from the Netherlands: (1) Utrecht Schizophrenia project (University Medical Center Utrecht) and (2) Genetic Risk and Outcome of Psychosis (GROUP) consortium.
dataset-of-origin.supporting_text: "Participants for the current study were selected from a large longitudinal sample based on two cohorts including patients with schizophrenia and healthy controls, the Utrecht Schizophrenia project and the Genetic Risk and Outcome of Psychosis (GROUP) consortium, in Utrecht, the Netherlands."

age.detail: Baseline age for schizophrenia patients (N=164) as reported in Table 1. Age range 16–70 years stated in Methods for the overall sample at baseline.
age.supporting_text: "Age, y: mean (SD): 29.52 (8.95)" [patients, baseline]; "a large longitudinal sample of patients with schizophrenia and healthy participants aged 16-70 years (at baseline)"

sex.detail: Table 1 reports 126 males (77%) out of 164 patients. Female N estimated as 164 − 126 = 38 (23.2%). Percentages recalculated to 1 decimal place: 126/164 = 76.8%, 38/164 = 23.2%.
sex.supporting_text: "Sex, n (%), males: 126 (77)" [Schizophrenia patients, Number of subjects: 164]
